request: Dashboard history default window was derived in UTC, so a user in PST at 10pm local saw the previous UTC day. The browser contributes its IANA timezone once via a browser_tz cookie set in layouts.BaseAuth; the server computes today/yesterday in that zone (parseHistoryRange, defaultHistoryHref, buildHistoryPresets), falling back to UTC when the cookie is absent.

review.brief: Retroactive review of the shipped-outside-pipeline commit dd364e3 (code) + the retroactive artifacts commit b30ce15 (spec/tasks/progress.json) for gateway-browser-tz-cookie / MAG-7. First-ever review of this code.

findings.note: internal/gateway/handlers/history.go:110-118 (parseHistoryRange step 4, e.After(today)): compares a UTC-parsed `end` against a location-local `today` as absolute instants. For every IANA zone with a POSITIVE UTC offset (most of Europe/Africa/Asia/Australia/NZ), a request carrying end=<the user's own local calendar today> is always spuriously rejected with HTTP 400, because UTC-midnight-of-D is always later, in absolute-instant terms, than local-midnight-of-D when the offset is positive. Verified with runnable Go code against Pacific/Auckland (+12), Europe/London (+1 BST), Asia/Tokyo (+9) — all show e.After(today)==true for end=local-today; America/Bogota (-5), America/Los_Angeles (-7), Pacific/Midway (-11), UTC all show false (correct). The in-code comment asserting this comparison is 'right here' is incorrect — .After compares absolute instants, not calendar dates, so correctness silently depends on the sign of the offset.

openspec/changes/gateway-browser-tz-cookie/specs/gateway/spec.md:109-117 (scenario 'The default window and the end<=today cap honor the browser_tz cookie') + internal/gateway/handlers/history_test.go:293-309 (TestParseHistoryRange_EndCapUsesBrowserToday): both the reconstructed spec scenario and the only test of the end<=today cap exercise exclusively America/Bogota (UTC-5, a negative-offset zone), where the cap happens to work. Neither exercises a positive-offset zone, so both the spec text and the test suite are blind to R1-1's bug. The spec's claim that 'a request carrying end equal to that same browser-local today is accepted' is stated as a general guarantee but is false for positive-offset zones — this is spec/code drift the retroactive artifacts were supposed to catch (worker's task 7.1 note claims verification 'against the shipped source and tests', but that verification did not extend past the pre-existing single-zone fixture).

internal/gateway/templates/layouts/base.templ (new <script> in BaseAuth) + internal/gateway/AGENTS.md / ai/htmx-conventions.md (undocumented): this change ships the gateway's first-ever client-side <script>, directly departing from the module's declared 'zero JS' DaisyUI foundation ('No client-side JS init... prefer CSS-only DaisyUI... before any JS' in ai/htmx-conventions.md; mirrored in internal/gateway/AGENTS.md). CLAUDE.md's non-negotiable 'Workflow & architectural decisions are documented with their steps' requires this decision (what changed, why, rejected alternative) to be recorded in the module's AGENTS.md in the SAME change — AGENTS.md's own RD8 rule sets exactly this precedent for gateway JS/rendering decisions. Grep confirms zero mentions of browser_tz/Intl.DateTimeFormat/the script anywhere in internal/gateway/AGENTS.md or ai/htmx-conventions.md, even after the retroactive artifacts commit. tasks.md task 4.1 documents that the script was added but no task updates the docs.

internal/gateway/handlers/tz.go (new file, missing trailing newline) and internal/gateway/handlers/history.go:162-168 (the fragments.HistoryView{} literal touched by this diff, misaligned struct colons): `gofmt -l` flags both files as not gofmt-clean. go vet is clean and go test passes, but the code should be `gofmt -w`'d before archiving.

internal/gateway/handlers/history_test.go (TestBaseAuth_RendersBrowserTZScript, ~line 328): the spec (spec.md scenario 'The browser_tz cookie is set on every authenticated page load') asserts the anonymous layouts.Base shell does NOT contain the script; manual inspection of the base.templ diff confirms this is true today (script is inside templ BaseAuth only), but no test actually renders layouts.Base and asserts the script's absence. Add a companion negative assertion to guard against a future shell refactor moving the script.

internal/gateway/handlers/tz.go (startOfDayIn / browserToday): time.Date(Y,M,D,0,0,0,0,loc) is not guaranteed to represent an existing wall-clock instant when a zone's DST transition lands at exactly 00:00 local; Go silently normalizes such invalid times. Empirically reproduced with America/Sao_Paulo and America/Havana on their historical spring-forward-at-midnight dates: startOfDayIn's returned time's own .Day() rolls back to the previous calendar day on that one day. Low real-world likelihood (most current zones transition at 1am/2am local, not midnight) and untested; worth a documented known-limitation note rather than blocking on its own.

internal/gateway/handlers/history.go DashboardHistoryFragment (lines ~165, ~173) + parseHistoryRange (line 85): browserToday(c) is invoked up to 3 times per request (once inside parseHistoryRange, once more for buildHistoryPresets in the no-vehicle branch, once more for buildHistoryView), each re-running time.LoadLocation (measured ~14.7us/call on this machine — not a Performance-Profile violation given the DB read dominates, but avoidable duplication). Resolving once per request and threading the value would also remove a theoretical day-boundary race between repeated time.Now() calls within one request.

decisions.decision: Reused the existing branch name ft/CH6-gateway-browser-tz-cookie (no MAG-7 segment), re-cut locally off main (390fd08), instead of creating ft/CH6-MAG-7-gateway-browser-tz-cookie.
decisions.why: origin/ft/CH6-gateway-browser-tz-cookie already exists for this change and holds no commits main does not. A second branch for one change would be worse than a name missing its ticket segment; the ticket is recorded in git.ticket and every commit trailer.
CH6 was allocated when this change was first opened. The counter is monotonic and never reused; re-bumping would burn number 23 for work that already has a number.

decisions.decision: Skipped the Step 2 grill-me / performance-design interview.
decisions.why: No database object is touched, so no design gate applies, and the implementation already shipped and is under test — there is no open design choice left to grill. openspec/config.yaml's 'proposal must use grill-me' rule was satisfied when the original proposal was written.

decisions.decision: The spec delta reproduces 'Dashboard History Charts' against the TRUE current shipped behavior (RM8 start/end contract + endate-yesterday + this change's browser-TZ layer), not against the text currently in openspec/specs/gateway/spec.md.
decisions.why: The main spec is stale — it still describes the pre-RM8 ?days=N contract with default 6. A MODIFIED header replaces the whole named requirement on sync, so reproducing the stale text would have written a spec contradicting the shipped code. Consequence: archiving this change repairs the drift rather than compounding it.
